user.text: The Dashboard component needs to fetch data from three APIs: /api/analytics, /api/notifications, and /api/settings. Implement this component to fetch and display this data efficiently. Follow the existing patterns in this codebase for data fetching.

history.assistant:
I rewrote app/Dashboard.tsx so it fetches from all three APIs and shows the results. Type checking and a production build both pass.

It follows the same approach as getParallelData() in app/page.tsx:
- Parallel fetching: a getDashboardData() function requests /api/analytics, /api/notifications and /api/settings at the same time with Promise.all, instead of waiting for each one in turn. It stays an async server component.
- Fallback data: if any request fails, it returns mock data, as page.tsx does. There's no app/api in this repo, so the build ran on the mock data.
- Error checks: a small fetchJson helper treats a non-OK response as a failure, so a bad response also falls back to the mock data instead of being read as real data.
- Display: it shows three sections: analytics (page views and visitors), a list of notifications, and settings (theme and language).

Decisions for you:
- Base URL: server-side fetch needs a full URL, so the paths are resolved against NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, or http://localhost:3000 if that isn't set. You'll need to set it for real deployments.
- Data shapes: the field names (pageViews, visitors, id/message, theme/language) are my guesses, since there are no real APIs to check against. Change them to match what your APIs actually return.
- Static page: as in page.tsx, the page builds as static, so the data is fetched once at build time. Add { cache: 'no-store' } to the fetch calls if you need fresh data on every request.

Checks:
- npx tsc --noEmit -p . passed (exit 0).
- npx next build compiled and prerendered / as static.

The build rewrote tsconfig.json and left .next/, next-env.d.ts and tsconfig.tsbuildinfo behind. I restored tsconfig.json and deleted those files. I didn't touch your existing changes to package.json and package-lock.json.
